title: The Still Room
description: An original guided rest practice. Five minutes is an accessible beginning, not a promise of sleep.

cues.title: Welcome to the Still Room
cues.text: Welcome to the Still Room. Find a position you can stay in comfortably. For these few minutes, nothing needs to be finished.

cues.title: Let the surface hold you
cues.text: Notice the support beneath you. The chair, the bed, or the ground can take some of your weight. You can keep your eyes open.

cues.title: An ordinary breath
cues.text: Notice one ordinary breath. Let it arrive without pulling it deeper. Let it leave without pushing. There is no breath to hold.

cues.title: A rhythm that fits you
cues.text: If it feels easy, let the breath become a little slower. Keep it small and comfortable. Your own rhythm is always enough.

cues.title: Nothing to force
cues.text: You do not need to follow the light or any count. If you feel uncomfortable, return to your usual breathing, or pause whenever you wish.

cues.title: You can let the view go
cues.text: Let your breathing keep its own rhythm now. If it feels comfortable, soften your gaze, or close your eyes. There is nothing more you need to watch.

cues.title: Begin with the feet
cues.text: Bring a little attention to your feet. Perhaps there is warmth, pressure, or very little to notice. There is no special feeling to find.

cues.title: Let the legs rest
cues.text: Notice your lower legs and your thighs. You can leave them as they are. If it is comfortable, let the surface beneath take their weight.

cues.title: Support beneath your body
cues.text: Notice the hips and the back. There may be points of contact with the surface beneath you. Nothing needs to be pressed down or held still.

cues.title: Hands with nothing to carry
cues.text: Let attention reach the hands and arms. They can rest wherever they are comfortable. For this moment, there is nothing they need to carry.

cues.title: A little less effort
cues.text: Notice the shoulders, the jaw, and the space around the eyes. Perhaps a little effort can soften. If it cannot, that is all right too.

cues.title: The body as a whole
cues.text: You may notice the body as a whole, breathing in its own rhythm. Rest with a sound, a point of contact, or simply this moment.

cues.title: Thoughts can come and go
cues.text: If thoughts arrive, you have not done anything wrong. Let them come and go. You can return gently to the feeling of support beneath you.

cues.title: Come back gently
cues.text: If you are ready, notice the room around you. Feel your hands and feet. Open your eyes whenever you wish. Take this pace with you.

cues.title: You can stay at rest
cues.text: You can stay at rest. There is no need to open your eyes or check the screen. Sleep may come, or this can simply be a quiet pause.

cues.title: A little more time
cues.text: There is a little more time here. Nothing new needs to happen. You may notice the support beneath you, with no need to change anything.

cues.title: A rhythm of your own
cues.text: Your breathing can keep its own rhythm. There is no count to follow now, and no particular size of breath that you need to make.

cues.title: Room for wandering
cues.text: If attention has wandered, that is part of being here. A thought can be present while the feeling of support is present too.

cues.title: Whatever is here
cues.text: There may be warmth, coolness, pressure, or very little to notice. Any of these is enough. Your experience does not need to match the words.

cues.title: Hands at rest
cues.text: Perhaps your hands are resting somewhere comfortable. They do not need a special position. There may be a little less work for them to do.

cues.title: Sounds around you
cues.text: Sounds may come and go around you. They need not become another task. If one catches your attention, returning to the body remains an option.

cues.title: An ordinary breath
cues.text: A comfortable exhalation may finish by itself. The next breath can arrive in its own time. Nothing needs holding, stretching, or making deliberately slower.

cues.title: The body as a whole
cues.text: You may be aware of the body as a whole, rather than finding each part. There is no need to search for a special sensation.

cues.title: A thought can wait
cues.text: If a thought asks for an answer, you do not have to solve it in this moment. Noticing that it arrived can be enough.

cues.title: Support remains
cues.text: The surface beneath you continues to be there. Some weight may already be resting on it. There is no need to test whether you feel relaxed.

cues.title: An imperfect pause
cues.text: Your face may feel as it does. Your shoulders may feel as they do. Comfort does not have to be complete for a pause to be allowed.

cues.title: No test to pass
cues.text: There may be moments of quiet and moments with many thoughts. Neither one decides how well you are doing. There is nothing here to pass.

cues.title: Your choices remain
cues.text: If any part of this is uncomfortable, changing position, opening your eyes, or stopping remains available. Rest can include making a small adjustment for yourself.

cues.title: Fewer words
cues.text: The words will become less frequent now. You may stay with an ordinary sound, the support beneath you, or simply the feeling of being here.

cues.title: A quiet pause
cues.text: Sleep may come, or this may remain a quiet pause. There is no need to wait for a sign, and no need to make either happen.

cues.title: Nothing more to follow
cues.text: There is nothing more to follow. The sound will soften on its own. If you wish, this can simply be a little time without another task.
